transcript_window.text: And we could do things now that we've never been able to do before.
The best encryption today still holds up against the best cracking tools around.
So can we create companies in such a manner than encrypt user data in such a way that an NSL would be pointless?
That's what Nick set out to do.
I learned about a philosophy called privacy by design.
And privacy by design means that when you're building something from like the first meeting you have when you're conceptualizing something, you think about how make it private.
I decided to sort of go off in this third direction of technology thinking that like, I believe in math, believe in believe in all this kind stuff.
I think that we as technologists can do something to make the problem better.
So he pivoted with his company, Calix.
Instead of it being an ISP, he turned it into a privacy focused company which created a bunch of things.
But the stuff that they're most notable for is the Calix OS and the Calix hotspot.
See, Nick wanted to help us many people as possible become more private and thought that the best way that could do this is to create a mobile operating system that is private by design.
He thought this would have the biggest impact since phones are ubiquitous, and everyone's online with them.
They're cheap and everywhere.
The two dominating mobile OS's today are Apple's and Google's Android.
And since we know they probably both comply with NSLs, any activity you do on there means the government can ask for it whenever they want without a warrant.
So what about an alternative phone OS that doesn't know anything about its users?
That way if the government sent an NSL to Calix, they wouldn't have a clue who's using their OS.
What they did is they took the OS, ripped out all the Google stuff, so it stopped sending telemetry to Google or even Calix for that matter.
I personally use Graphine OS on my phone which is very similar.
There's no trace of Google on my phone and I love it.
So funded, they rely on donations.
But they also have a hotspot service at the offer which I actually paid for in use.
basically give them a yearly donation and they send you a Wi -Fi hotspot that works good for a year.
And the hotspot is not connected to my name.
I paid for it anonymously using cash at DEF CON and the only thing they have on me is my email address which is a burger email.
And this little hotspot has been doing great for me for years and it's going really well for Calix too.
